answer: Suppose admission runs through a glacier queue: each candidate identity is frozen into a cohort, and the cohort melts only after its median delivery rate matches the incumbent population's over a full season. Before melt, members hold beacon status only: they may sign and deliver but cannot receive emission, so flooding clones yields frozen capital and no income. Each mesa grade of the maturity ladder doubles the collateral a clone needs to repeat the freeze, while honest agents walk it once. Queue length is public, so a farm prices its cost first.
